title: OpenAI says ChatGPT handles a fifth of Google's search-like query volume — Taboola revenue falls 6.9%
subtitle: OpenAI's Adam Fry tells an interviewer that ChatGPT queries that trigger a web search are now roughly 20% of Google's volume; the same day, Taboola blames AI for a drop in impressions.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI's head of search, Adam Fry, told interviewer Alex Kantrowitz that the volume of ChatGPT queries that trigger a web search is now roughly one-fifth of Google's total search volume. Fry explicitly framed the figure as a volume comparison, not a market share claim. The same day, November 4, the ad-tech company Taboola told investors its quarterly revenue had fallen 6.9%, attributing the decline to fewer ad impressions and the growing share of user questions answered by AI summaries before any click leaves the chat.

Independent measurements of the same phenomenon differ widely. An Ahrefs-based analysis of outbound clicks puts ChatGPT at under 1% of Google's search volume by that measure. Peec AI's blended estimate falls between 4% and 12%. The three numbers measure different things — total search-like queries versus outgoing clicks versus a blended traffic estimate — and are not directly comparable. That spread is itself the point: nobody outside OpenAI has access to the full query log, and the industry still lacks a shared definition of 'an AI search.'

The Taboola data point matters because it moves the story from OpenAI's self-report to a counterparty's audited quarterly filing. Content aggregators and ad networks sit downstream of search engines; when upstream query patterns shift, their revenue curves reveal the shift before any press release does. Publishers, agencies, and SEO vendors are now building dashboards that treat ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini as named referral channels. Expect a lot of M&A in the AI search measurement space over the next two quarters.

Takeaway for learners: when a company reports a metric about itself, look for an independent party whose balance sheet moves in the same direction. OpenAI's 20% claim on its own is marketing. OpenAI's 20% claim plus Taboola's 6.9% revenue drop is a market signal. The rule is general: triangulate self-reported platform numbers against downstream economic data before you treat them as true.
